label: Copy phase, later recall steps, input token is w/x/l/h/m/i
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (100% of mass; essentially never on original tokens or <DEL>). Rate rises with recall position: near zero for recall_idx 0-1, ~9% at 3, 18-32% from 4 onward, and highest in long sequences (L=9 holds 47% of mass). Within the copy phase the input token is the main factor: w (29% rate, 25% of mass) and x (25%, 21% of mass) are strongest, then l, h, m, i, with weaker graded contributions from r, n, d, s and others. The previous token adds a smaller effect (v, a, q, t, y before the current token raise it). The top activations are w or x fed back at mid-to-late copy steps. The predicate (copy, recall_idx>=3, in_tok in {w,x,l,h,m,i}) gets dev F1 0.62 and mass recall 0.77. The token preference looks graded, not a clean set: adding r/n/d raises mass recall to 0.85 but lowers precision. It is also not active on every such step (precision about 0.6).
